rationale: The Parkinson diet cohort recorded mango without a graded insomnia result. Other mango studies measured a sleep item or omitted sleep. Isolated myrcene altered barbiturate-induced sleep in animals, with opposite results under different schedules, and none of those comparisons administered raw mango. The exact clinical claim remains open.

Two small dried rosemary capsule trials outside Parkinson disease reported lower depression scores. Fresh-derived extract beverage studies omitted clinical depression. The three-extract trial gives an inconclusive overall BDI-II comparison and a favorable subgroup with unresolved reporting details. An injected isolated compound changed mouse behavior only. The minimal lean against the claim rests on the human capsule studies.

Several randomized human oral cinnamon studies favor lower measured pain, including bark powder in migraine and primary menstrual pain. The Parkinson case used multiple treatments. Isolated beta-caryophyllene reduced some mouse pain responses and gave inconclusive results on others. Differences in clinical pain and culinary exposure limit the favorable lean.

Standalone cinnamaldehyde maze findings were inconclusive in several experiments. Isolated injected beta-caryophyllene affected mouse behavior, and the human stress and Parkinson survey data give no result attributable to ground cinnamon. Evidence direction remains unresolved for the frozen claim.

The closest oral ground-pepper add-on gave inconclusive chronic-pain results. Human blends, exercise and topical trials leave the cracked-pepper effect unresolved. Isolated piperine and beta-caryophyllene trials measured animal reflexes, with both favorable and inconclusive results depending on the assay. The clinical claim remains open.

One dried-thyme trial reported more students in its normal-range HADS anxiety category. The reported baseline spread, categorical cutoffs and registry design limit interpretation. A wild-thyme extract trial is inconclusive. Isolated oral carvacrol and an injected derivative altered mouse behavior, with reporting gaps. The human thyme comparison supports a minimal favorable lean.

A depleted Syrian oregano comparator study gives no contrast against absence of oregano. A dried leaf infusion reduced mouse exploration alongside reduced motor performance. Isolated carvacrol, beta-caryophyllene and a synthetic derivative affected other mouse behaviors under different routes, with conflicting reporting. Direction remains unresolved for dried oregano and Parkinson anxiety.

Parkinson interview reports and controlled whole-rhizome comparisons support a minimal favorable lean. Separate extract trials give favorable, inconclusive and inconsistent pain results. The nerve injury study concerns an isolated compound and other plant oil and leaves its immobility data unresolved. The severity effect of grated ginger remains indirect.

The blinded healthy-volunteer leaf tea study gave no clear separation in sleep reports. Favorable inhaled oil findings had design limits. Isolated myrcene changed barbiturate-induced sleep under injection, oral and inhaled conditions, with opposite associations across acute and repeated oral schedules. The leaf-food comparison in Parkinson insomnia remains open.

Sweet-basil leaf extract reduced insomnia scores in menopausal participants, while an independent dried-basil postpartum trial was inconclusive. Isolated myrcene animal reports used drug-induced sleep and varied by exposure schedule. A minimal favorable lean relies on the human basil extract comparison and limited transfer to fresh basil and Parkinson disease.

Two independent urinary infection cohorts reported lower symptom scores after a lovage-root, rosemary and centaury product. One is uncontrolled and the other compares the blend with fosfomycin. The available urgency results concern symptom severity, and neither cohort measured episodes after dried lovage leaf in Parkinson disease.
